title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Vietnam: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Vietnam: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a Vietnamese citizen dies in Viet Nam, immediate administration centers on medical or police death clearance, civil registration at the Commune-level People's Committee within 15 days, social insurance claims under Law on Social Insurance No. 41/2024/QH15 (effective 1 July 2025), and estate settlement under the 2015 Civil Code. For cross-border documents, note an important recent legal shift: the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention entered into force for Viet Nam on 11 September 2026 under Decree No. 293/2026/ND-CP, replacing consular legalization for most partner states except Germany, Austria, and Czechia, which lodged Article 12 objections. This checklist outlines the verified legal and administrative steps across official Vietnamese portals and HCCH filings [1][2][5][6].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification and police clearance
steps.html:
• Death at a hospital or medical facility: The treating hospital or health station issues the Medical Death Notice (Giay bao tu) required before civil death registration and cemetery or crematorium booking [1][10].
  • Death at home or sudden/unexpected death: For natural deaths at home, the family requests a death confirmation from local commune authorities or the medical station; for sudden, accidental, or unexplained deaths, contact local police immediately so investigators and forensic examiners can determine the cause of death and issue clearance for body release [1][10].
  • Confirm matching personal data: Verify that the deceased's full name, Citizen Identity Card (CCCD) number, household registration details, and date and place of death match civil records prior to filing [1][10].

steps.title: Civil death registration and death certificate extracts
steps.html:
• Fifteen-day statutory deadline: Under Law on Civil Status No. 60/2014/QH13 (referenced on both Chính phủ and ILO NATLEX repositories), relatives or responsible persons must register the death within 15 days from the date of death [1][2].
  • Filing office: Submit the Giay bao tu (or equivalent official death confirmation), the informant's Citizen Identity Card, and the deceased's identity documents at the Commune-level People's Committee (Uy ban nhan dan cap xa) at the deceased's last permanent residence (or place of death if residence cannot be determined), accessed through Government Portal of Viet Nam (Civil Status and Social Insurance Laws) [1][10].
  • Certificate and multiple extracts: The civil registrar enters the death into the Civil Status Register and issues the official Death Certificate Extract (Trich luc khai tu); request several certified extracts immediately for banks, Vietnam Social Security (VSS), notaries, and land offices [1][10].

steps.title: Burial, cremation, repatriation, and the 2026 Apostille framework
steps.html:
• Burial and cremation permits: Local cemetery boards and crematoria require the Giay bao tu or Trich luc khai tu alongside local public-health and municipal clearances; if transporting remains abroad, obtain embalming, non-infectious medical, and customs certificates plus passport cancellation [10].
  • Hague Apostille in force since 11 September 2026: Viet Nam's accession to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention entered into force on 11 September 2026 (implemented domestically by Decree No. 293/2026/ND-CP), designating Consular Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Viet Nam (MOFA) in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City Department of Foreign Affairs as Competent Authorities issuing Apostilles [5][6][7][8].
  • Mandatory exception for Germany, Austria, and Czechia: Under Article 12(2) notifications published by the Hague Conference on Private International Law, Germany (20 May 2026), Austria (19 June 2026), and Czechia (2 July 2026) objected to Viet Nam's accession, so public documents exchanged between Viet Nam and those three countries do not qualify for an Apostille and still require consular legalization through MOFA and the relevant embassy [6][9].

steps.title: Social insurance benefits, reference level, and ID closures
steps.html:
• Funeral allowance under the 2024 Social Insurance Law: Under Law on Social Insurance No. 41/2024/QH15 (effective 1 July 2025, linked via Government Portal of Viet Nam (Civil Status and Social Insurance Laws) and administered by Vietnam Social Security (VSS)), the statutory calculation benchmark transitioned to the reference level (muc tham chieu), and the individual handling the funeral of a qualifying contributor, pensioner, or monthly work-injury recipient receives a lump-sum funeral allowance equal to 10 times the reference level in the month of death [3][4].
  • Monthly vs. lump-sum survivorship allowance: Vietnam Social Security (VSS) pays monthly survivorship allowances to eligible dependent spouses, minor children, or parents where contribution thresholds (such as 15 years of compulsory contributions or pensioner status) are met, or a lump-sum survivorship allowance calculated using the reference level active in the month of death [3][4].
  • Cancel personal documents and notify banks: Notify employers, health insurance (BHYT) offices, banks, and Citizen Identity / passport authorities using Trich luc khai tu so accounts are frozen pending succession settlement [1][10].

steps.title: Estate administration, notarized division, and inheritance rules
steps.html:
• Succession under the 2015 Civil Code: Under Civil Code No. 91/2015/QH13 published in Government Official Gazette of Viet Nam (Cong bao Chinh phu), estates pass according to a valid will (subject to mandatory reserved shares for minor or incapacitated children, spouses, and parents) or statutory intestate succession orders [11][12].
  • Notarized declaration or division of inheritance: Co-heirs commonly execute an Agreement on Division of Estate or Declaration of Acceptance of Inheritance before a public or private notary office (subject to the modernized procedures of Law on Notarization No. 46/2024/QH15, effective 1 July 2025) after mandatory public posting at the Commune-level People's Committee before transferring land-use right certificates (Red Books) or bank balances [13].
  • Tax and cross-border estate steps: Although direct inheritance transfers between close statutory relatives generally enjoy personal income tax exemptions on real estate and inherited assets upon proper tax declaration, inheritance disputes go to the People's Court under civil procedure rules [11].
